questions.text: Why is handling missing values important in machine learning?
options: Missing values improve model accuracy
Most ML algorithms cannot handle missing values directly
Missing values reduce computational cost
Missing values are always errors that must be removed
questions.explanation: Most machine learning algorithms cannot handle missing values directly and will throw errors or produce incorrect results. You must either remove rows/columns with missing values (which can lead to data loss) or fill them in using imputation techniques. Proper handling of missing values is crucial for building accurate and reliable models.

questions.text: What is the main advantage of imputation over deletion when handling missing values?
options: Imputation is always more accurate
Imputation allows you to retain more data
Imputation is faster to compute
Imputation removes outliers
questions.explanation: The main advantage of imputation is that it allows you to retain more data. Deletion (removing rows or columns with missing values) can lead to significant data loss, especially when missing values are common. Imputation fills in reasonable estimates for missing values, preserving your dataset size and potentially important patterns in the data.

questions.text: When should you use median imputation instead of mean imputation?
options: When you have categorical data
When the feature has a skewed distribution or outliers
When you have time series data
When missing values are at the beginning of the dataset
questions.explanation: Median imputation is preferred when the feature has a skewed distribution or contains outliers. The median is robust to outliers and extreme values, while the mean can be heavily influenced by them. For example, if you have income data with a few very high values, the median provides a more representative central value than the mean.

questions.text: What type of data is mode imputation most appropriate for?
options: Continuous numerical features with normal distribution
Categorical features or discrete numerical features
Time series data with temporal ordering
Features with many outliers
questions.explanation: Mode imputation is most appropriate for categorical features (like color, category, or type) or discrete numerical features (like number of bedrooms). The mode is the most frequently occurring value, which makes sense for categorical data. For continuous numerical features with many unique values, mode imputation is less meaningful since no single value may be representative.

questions.text: What is forward fill imputation and when is it most useful?
options: Filling missing values with the mean of future values
Replacing missing values with the last observed value, useful for time series
Filling missing values with the most common value in the dataset
Using machine learning to predict missing values
questions.explanation: Forward fill (also called 'carry forward') replaces missing values with the last observed value before the missing entry. This is most useful for time series data where values change slowly over time and temporal ordering matters. For example, if a sensor reading is missing, using the previous reading is often a reasonable estimate. However, it only works for ordered data and cannot fill the first values.

questions.text: What does MCAR (Missing Completely At Random) mean?
options: Missing values occur in a random pattern across the dataset
Missing values are unrelated to any observed or unobserved data
Missing values depend on the observed data
Missing values are caused by measurement errors
questions.explanation: MCAR (Missing Completely At Random) means that the probability of a value being missing is completely unrelated to any observed or unobserved data. For example, if survey responses are missing because some forms were randomly lost in the mail, that's MCAR. Understanding the type of missingness (MCAR, MAR, or MNAR) helps you choose the most appropriate imputation strategy and understand potential biases.

questions.text: What is a major disadvantage of mean/median imputation?
options: It increases the variance in the data
It only works for categorical data
It reduces variance and can distort relationships between features
It is too computationally expensive
questions.explanation: A major disadvantage of mean and median imputation is that they reduce variance in the data. By replacing missing values with a single central value, you're artificially making the data more uniform. This can distort relationships between features and lead to underestimated standard errors and overly confident statistical inferences. More sophisticated methods like KNN imputation or multiple imputation can better preserve variance.

questions.text: True or False: You should always use the same imputation strategy for all features in your dataset.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: False. Different features may require different imputation strategies based on their data type, distribution, and the nature of the missing values. For example, you might use median imputation for skewed numerical features, mode imputation for categorical features, and forward fill for time series features. The best practice is to analyze each feature individually and choose the most appropriate imputation method based on domain knowledge and the data characteristics.
